text:
Michael Rasmussen's season has become a study in how little the scoresheet can tell you. He has 1 goal in 22 games and none in his last twelve, and his ice time has slid with it: under nine minutes in two of his last three games, and about 13 a night lately against 15 for the season.

The process is better than that. The Red Wings have taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, better than when he sits, and he has 4.6 expected goals of his own to show for that 1 goal. Detroit has scored 10.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which is mostly bad luck and usually swings back. He's a 6'6" checking center who kills penalties and blocks shots (29 so far), and Evolving-Hockey rated him around replacement level last season, so goals were never the whole job. Our numbers project about 9 goals. The thing to watch is whether the minutes come back before the bounces do.
headline: Michael Rasmussen's minutes are slipping with the goals
